title: Warn before saving nsec in profile name or bio
body:
## Summary
Users can accidentally paste an `nsec` into the profile name or bio fields. The app should warn before saving when either field appears to contain a private key.

## Why
An `nsec` in profile text is a serious footgun. Even if we do not fully block it yet because there may be edge cases, showing a warning is a low-cost safety check.

## Proposed behavior
- Detect when the profile name or bio looks like an `nsec`
- Show a clear warning before saving
- Let the final UX decision stay open: hard block by default vs allow with explicit override

## Notes
Arguably this should be disabled entirely, but a warning is the obvious minimum safeguard.

title: Audio messages

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
# Context

We want so send and receive audio messages. We need to support two cases:
- Audio message sent as an imeta tag (as another media attachment) -> we don't want to send audio messages this way but for interoperability purposes, we have display the ones we receive from other marmot clients. 🦀 Here we need an easy way to know that it is an audio file and not an image, but we can have a workaround by checking mime types
- Audio messages sent as an event (a message where the message itself is the audio, not as an imeta tag and without text content), following https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/94.md 🦀  Here we need a MIP specification for this new kind of events inside the chat .... but maybe we can still use the same method that we currently use to send messages? not 100% sure

🎨 We need design to decide how this audios will be displayed in both cased and how the audio recording UX will be.

title: Local AI transcription for audio messages

labels.name: Idea 💡
labels.description: Ideas of changes so we don't forget to re evaluate later

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Problem

White Noise already has `#422` for audio messages, but there is not yet a dedicated issue for private, on-device transcription of those messages.

If White Noise adds voice notes, local transcription would make them more accessible and searchable without sending audio to a third-party service.

## Proposed solution

Add local AI transcription for audio messages / voice notes, as a layer on top of `#422`.

A concrete direction:

- use an on-device Whisper-based speech-to-text pipeline instead of a remote API
- download models on demand and store them locally, with clear size / quality tradeoffs
- expose model management in settings (download, delete, selected model)
- support automatic language detection for incoming audio messages
- show a transcript inline for audio messages, with timestamped segments if possible
- keep transcription optional and explicit, not always-on magic
- avoid any remote transcription service

Useful implementation details from Vector:

- it uses `whisper-rs` / local Whisper inference rather than a hosted API
- it caches downloaded models locally and lets the user manage them
- it exposes several model sizes with rough RAM / performance expectations
- it returns segmented transcript data with timestamps, which makes playback + transcript seeking much nicer
- it keeps the whole flow on-device, which preserves the privacy story

## Alternatives considered

- rely on OS-level speech APIs: easier in some cases, but less consistent across platforms and often less auditable
- send audio to a hosted speech-to-text service: simpler to ship, but a bad privacy tradeoff for White Noise
- skip transcription entirely: simpler, but it leaves voice notes much less accessible and searchable

## Additional context

Translation should stay separate under `#398`. This issue is only about local transcription for audio messages.

I think `marmot-protocol/whitenoise` is the right repo for this request instead of `whitenoise-rs`, because this is a user-facing feature spanning UX, settings, model management, and Rust integration.

Reference repo:
- https://github.com/VectorPrivacy/Vector

body:
# Motivation

I was talking with a friend (who is not privacy concerned at all) but she told me that something she missed about whatsapp was a way to have translations in the same messaging app.

Her use case is that she works with people that come to our country but that speak other languages, bad spanish and bad english so it's really hard to communicate.  She has a lot of trouble chatting with them and has to copy paste every message into translation app. 


She would like to see the original message in the original language so that she can learn a bit, but have the option to see the translation in the same chat bubble.

I think tit would be cool to have different features from traditional messaging apps so that we can onboard users with more reasons than privacy (cause that friend for example doe not care)

# The Challenge

Adding translations in a private way. We definitely don't want to use a third party service, cause there is no point on having E2EE to then send every message to a third party 😅 . It would be nice to run a local translation model in the phone.

title: Adopt whitenoise-rs arch-refactor: per-account sessions replace the god object
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/78dc0ac6367f959479dea509953a057bf83f10b1d64cbb0307e7f2dd507e5a91.jpg)

## What changed

`whitenoise-rs` is now pinned to the `arch-refactor` branch (sha `eefe3fe9...`). That branch removed `Whitenoise::get_instance()` and split the god object into one `AccountSession` per account.

## Shim layer

`rust/src/api/mod.rs` holds a private `tokio::sync::OnceCell<Arc<Whitenoise>>` populated by `initialize_whitenoise`. Two helpers:

- `wn() -> &'static Whitenoise` for the few global calls that remain (login, all-accounts, app settings).
- `wn_session(&pubkey) -> Arc<AccountSession>` for everything else.

Init goes through `OnceCell::get_or_try_init`, so two concurrent `initialize_whitenoise` calls share one underlying `Whitenoise::ensure_initialized` run.

## Call-site migration

About 95 sites in `rust/src/api/` moved off the deleted facades onto `session.<ops>()`:

- `session.membership().for_group(&gid)` for accept / decline / archive / unarchive / mute / unmute / pin / mark-read / clear-chat.
- `session.groups()` for visible / by-id / members / admins / create / add-members / remove-members / leave / update-data.
- `session.groups().media()` for upload / download / image-path.
- `session.drafts()`, `session.chat_list()`, `session.mute_list()`, `session.social()`, `session.key_packages()`, `session.push()`, `session.settings()`.

`get_chat_summary` now searches both active and archived chat lists so archived chats render correctly (master commit 8135cbe's intent, under the new API).

## Other adjustments

- `MuteListEntry.account_pubkey` is gone upstream; the shim now passes the pubkey through `MuteListEntry::from_entry`.
- `account.relays(...)` and `user.key_package_*(...)` now take `&Arc<SharedServices>`; the shim passes `&whitenoise.shared`.
- `AccountGroup::get` is gone; the shim uses `session.membership().for_group(&gid).get_or_create(None)`.
- The new `subscribe_to_group_state` from master switched from `Whitenoise::get_instance()` to `wn()`.

## Status

Bridge regenerated. `just precommit` is green. The colony of marmots can stop fetching from the one big burrow and head to their own.

---

Built against `whitenoise-rs` arch-refactor sha `eefe3fe927b53c9c890c2ac1bbc19b269fb41382`.

title: Support NIP-46 remote signing for iOS users
body:
## Summary

White Noise should support NIP-46 (Nostr Remote Signing) so iOS users can sign events without pasting their nsec directly into the app. This is the standard Nostr protocol for delegating signing to a remote signer or bunker service.

## TLDR: How NIP-46 Works

NIP-46 defines a protocol where a **client** (White Noise) communicates with a **remote signer** (a bunker or dedicated signing app) over Nostr relays using encrypted kind `24133` events.

**The flow:**

1. User connects White Noise to a remote signer via a `bunker://` URI (provided by their signer) or a `nostrconnect://` URI (generated by White Noise).
2. White Noise generates a disposable keypair for encrypted communication with the signer.
3. When White Noise needs to sign an event, it sends a `sign_event` request (NIP-44 encrypted) to the remote signer over relays.
4. The remote signer signs and returns the signed event. The user's nsec never touches the client.

**Available methods:** `connect`, `sign_event`, `ping`, `get_public_key`, `nip04_encrypt`, `nip04_decrypt`, `nip44_encrypt`, `nip44_decrypt`

**Connection strings look like:**
- Signer-initiated: `bunker://<signer-pubkey>?relay=wss://relay.example.com&secret=<random>`
- Client-initiated: `nostrconnect://<client-pubkey>?relay=wss://relay.example.com&secret=<random>`

Full spec: https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/46.md

## Why This Matters for iOS

On Android, users have [Amber](https://github.com/greenart7c3/Amber) for local signing (NIP-55). iOS has no equivalent native signer app. NIP-46 is the path for iOS users to keep their keys off-device by connecting to:

- **nsec.app** — browser-based remote signer
- **nsecBunker** — self-hosted or SaaS bunker
- **Any NIP-46 compatible signer**

Without NIP-46, iOS users must paste their nsec directly into White Noise, which increases the attack surface. NIP-46 was designed to solve exactly this problem: minimizing the number of systems that touch private keys.

## Proposed UX

1. Login screen offers "Connect with Remote Signer" alongside the existing nsec input.
2. User can either:
   - Paste a `bunker://` connection string from their signer, or
   - Scan a QR code containing the bunker URI.
3. White Noise establishes the NIP-46 session and calls `get_public_key` to learn the user's identity.
4. All subsequent signing happens transparently via the remote signer.

## Related

- NIP-46 spec: https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/46.md
- Existing Amber issue: #289
- List of NIP-46 clients/signers: https://github.com/blackcoffeexbt/awesome-nip46-remote-nostr-signing-clients

title: [Feature]: Nip-46

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/06ab8c2d071a807e1f80bfc46dfbaa659cd784777433fbb7b7abae36f80644b1.png)

## Problem

Currently, support exists for Amber via NIP-55, but that is primarily useful for Android users. This creates an uneven experience across platforms, since iOS users do not have an equivalent way to use an external signer through the app.

It also limits future platform consistency. Once a desktop app is released, having external signer support would be very helpful.

## Proposed solution

Add support for NIP-46 remote signing, similar in spirit to the Amber (NIP-55) support already added.

This would allow users to connect to a compatible external signer and approve signing requests without requiring direct key storage in the app. The goal is to provide a platform-independent signing flow so Android, iOS, and eventually desktop users can all benefit from external signer support.

title: [Feature]: Android auto-update flow — verify, download, and install signed Zapstore releases from inside the app

labels.name: Idea 💡
labels.description: Ideas of changes so we don't forget to re evaluate later

body:
## Summary

Build on the update-detection notification in #621 by adding an end-to-end auto-update flow on Android: detect a new release, verify the publisher signature, verify the APK SHA-256, download, and hand off to the OS install flow.

## Scope

**Android only.** iOS app updates are handled by the App Store and TestFlight (see #621 for details). This issue does not apply to iOS.

## Why

#621 tells the user a new release exists. They still have to leave the app, open Zapstore (or another channel), find White Noise, and tap update. For sideloaded users this is friction that keeps stale builds in the wild. A first-class self-update flow inside White Noise closes the loop.

## Flow

1. **Detect**: same Zapstore relay query as #621 (`kinds: [30063]`, `authors: [<whitenoise-pubkey>]`).
2. **Resolve assets**: read referenced kind `3063` file metadata events to get APK URL, SHA-256, and architecture (`arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64`). Pick the asset matching the device ABI.
3. **Verify event signatures**: confirm the kind:30063 release event and the kind:3063 asset event are signed by the pinned White Noise publisher pubkey. Drop anything that fails.
4. **Download APK** to app-private storage with a progress indicator.
5. **Verify APK hash**: SHA-256 of the downloaded file must match the `x` tag from the kind:3063 event. Fail loud if it doesn't — never hand a mismatched APK to the installer.
6. **Hand off to OS installer**: launch `Intent.ACTION_VIEW` with the APK URI (via FileProvider) and `application/vnd.android.package-archive`. The OS shows its own install confirmation; the user approves.
7. **On success**: the OS replaces the running app. Done.

## Permissions research

To install an APK programmatically on modern Android, the app must hold:

- **`REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES`** (declared in manifest, granted per-app by the user via "Install unknown apps" / "Allow from this source"). This is mandatory since API 26 (Android 8). Without it, the install Intent fails.

The user grant is a system-level toggle the user enables once per source app. The app cannot grant it itself; it can only deep-link the user to the relevant Settings screen if not yet granted (`Settings.ACTION_MANAGE_UNKNOWN_APP_SOURCES`).

No `INSTALL_PACKAGES` (signature/system-only permission, not for third-party apps) and no root required. The flow is the same one Zapstore, F-Droid, and Obtainium already use.

**On GrapheneOS**: same `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES` model applies. GrapheneOS adds no extra restriction here, but the user may have explicitly disabled "Install unknown apps" for White Noise — handle the denial gracefully and link them to settings.

**Play Store**: this flow is incompatible with Play Store policy (Play disallows apps that install other apps via package installer except for narrow developer-tool exceptions). If White Noise ever ships on Play, the auto-update path must be disabled in the Play build variant. The Zapstore / sideload variant retains it.

## Open questions

- Should the auto-update prompt the user before downloading, or just before installing? Suggest: prompt before download (data cost transparency), required user tap before install (OS shows the install dialog anyway).
- What happens on download failure or hash mismatch? Suggest: hard-fail with a clear in-app error; never silently retry with degraded verification.
- Background download or foreground only? **Recommend: background download.** Once a release is detected and signature-verified, fetch the APK in the background so the user does not wait on the network when they tap update. APK sizes are small (tens of MB) and the cost is a one-time download per release, so bandwidth impact is minimal. Respect Android's data-saver setting (skip background fetch on metered connections when data saver is on); fall back to on-demand foreground download in that case. The OS install dialog still requires an explicit user tap before anything is replaced.
- Should we offer "skip this version" so users can defer specific releases? Suggest: yes, but never let them skip if they fall 3+ behind (matches escalation in #621).
- Build variant flag (`flavor=zapstore` vs `flavor=play`) to compile-out the self-update path on Play Store builds.

## Dependencies

- Blocks on #621. The detection and pubkey-pinning work there is the foundation here. Land #621 first; this issue layers download + install on top.

## Test platform

GrapheneOS, with `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES` granted and revoked, to confirm both happy and denied paths.

## Cross-reference

- Notification-only sibling: #621

body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/f3757fc28c0f4949a066f4338316f1d54ce148f70322d769352aa5b94cafb459.png) Closes #483. Returning to the chat list flashed a loading spinner because go_router's `goNamed` disposes `ChatListScreen`, and on pop the `useChatList` hook re-subscribed to the stream with no cached data. So every back-navigation looked like a cold start. Cache the chat-list map (per pubkey + archived) and the blocked-pubkeys set (per pubkey) at module scope so they outlive widget disposal. `isLoading` now gates on whether an initial snapshot was ever received, not on the current stream's connection state. A remount renders the cached marmots immediately and updates lazily as new stream events arrive. Regression test in `test/hooks/use_chat_list_test.dart` reproduces the bug (fails on old code, passes on the fix). Screen-level test in `test/screens/chat_list_screen_test.dart` locks in the user-flow behavior. Test-side cache reset is wired into `MockWnApi.reset()` so individual test files keep their existing setUp. `just precommit` passes. Coverage 99.36%. --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Chat list preserves cached chats when returning from a conversation, eliminating spinner flicker and unnecessary loading. * Blocked-contacts and chat-list caching prevent redundant fetches, improving navigation speed and reducing data usage. * **Tests** * Added/updated tests to cover cached chat behavior and remount scenarios; test teardown now clears related cached state. [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/641)

title: Replace public follows with private contact lists
body:
# Context
"Contacts" in a messaging app are expected to be private. Today, adding a contact in Sloth updates the user's public Nostr follow list, which is visible to anyone and affects the user's follow list in every other Nostr client. This is a fundamental privacy mismatch: "contact" implies a private relationship, but the underlying action is fully public. For that reason, we decided to rename contacts to follows #592 

# Proposed solution
 Introduce a separate, encrypted contact list The list could be initially seeded from the user's existing follows to avoid an empty list at start problem, with the user able to edit it independently going forward.

Once this is in place, the UI wording should be changed back to contact, as "Add as contact" / "Remove as contact" would again be accurate and private, unlike the current public-follow-backed implementation.
 
⚠️ 🦀   This issue needs rust changes first.
  
**Notes**
- This is not a priority at this time but is the correct long-term direction.
- Related to the wording fix of #592 
-  A MIP may be needed depending on the chosen encrypted contact list format.

title: Render Markdown inline and support .md file previews in groups

labels.name: Idea 💡
labels.description: Ideas of changes so we don't forget to re evaluate later

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

body:
## Idea

Support Markdown rendering in two places:

1. **Inline messages** - Render Markdown formatting (bold, italic, code blocks, links, lists) directly in chat messages.
2. **Uploaded .md files** - When a `.md` file is shared in a group, render a preview of its contents instead of showing it as a raw file download.

This would make group conversations more readable and useful for sharing structured content, documentation, and notes.

title: [Bug]: Bug report screen stays open with filled text after successful submission
body:
## Summary

After submitting a bug report, a green toast confirms success — but the screen stays open with the report text still filled in. Users have no clear signal the submission worked beyond the brief toast, so they tend to submit again thinking it failed.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Settings → Report a Bug
2. Fill in the report text
3. Submit
4. Observe: success toast appears, but screen remains open with text intact

## Expected Behavior

After a successful submission, either:
- Navigate back to the settings screen, or
- Clear the text field so the screen is visibly reset

## Environment

- Platform: GrapheneOS

title: fix: load chat summary via point query so archived chats render correctly
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/5815cb9d270870cfe44a5a5ea958e91422a633c7c2050e363739950f90d4b994.jpg) ## What this fixes Two archive-related bugs share one root cause: - #650: chat header shows "Unknown User" when the chat is archived - #651: the "this user is blocked" banner is missing in archived chats ## Root cause `get_chat_summary` looked up a single chat by calling `whitenoise.get_chat_list(&account).find(...)`. The upstream `get_chat_list()` filters archived chats out, so for any archived chat the lookup returned `ApiError::Other { "Chat not found" }`. Flutter caught the error, `ChatSummary.data` was null, and two render paths broke: - `header.displayName` was null, so the chat header fell back to `unknownUser` - `peerPubkey` was null, which forces `isBlocked = false`, so the blocked banner never showed ## The fix Use the upstream point-query `whitenoise.get_chat_list_item(&account, &group_id)`. It returns the chat regardless of archive state. The upstream docstring at `chat_list.rs:279-316` documents this distinction between list and point queries. One file, three insertions, eight deletions. ## Rebase note You will need to rebase this PR once #649 merges (or I'll just rebase that if this merges first). ## Verification Reporter repro from #651: 1. Block a user 2. Archive that chat 3. Open the chat from the archive list 4. Blocked banner appears 5. Chat header shows the contact's name Fixes #650 Fixes #651 --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance Improvements** * Optimized chat summary retrieval for faster chat data access. [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/653)

title: [Bug]: Blocked dialog box doesn't show when a chat is in the archive
body:
## Summary

I don't get the in-chat dialog box that tells me the user is blocked when the chat is in the archive

## Steps to reproduce

1. Block a user
2. send that chat to archive
3. open archive and open the chat
4. no "this user is blocked" dialog shows. 
5. move chat back to main chat list (unarchive)
6. Blocked dialog shows in the chat now

## Expected behavior

We should see the blocked user dialog in both the normal chat list and the archived chat list
